name: dilute concentration without droplets (control)
question: Does the dilute concentration of a droplet-forming species return to its set point after a step of its supply, and through which variable?

provenance.source: droplet growth by Gibbs-Thomson exchange with the dilute phase: I. M. Lifshitz and V. V. Slyozov, J. Phys. Chem. Solids 19, 35 (1961); C. Wagner, Z. Elektrochem. 65, 581 (1961); turnover of the droplet material inside the droplets: D. Zwicker, A. A. Hyman and F. Juelicher, Phys. Rev. E 92, 012317 (2015); mean field for identical droplets

assumptions: dimensionless: u = c/c_sat, r = R/R0, time in rho R0^2/(D c_sat), j the supply, kappa1 the removal in the dilute phase, kappa2 the turnover inside the droplets, Gamma = 4 pi n R0^3 rho/c_sat, eps the capillary length over R0
no dense phase: the supply is removed only in the dilute phase
the step of the input: the supply j from 0.12 to 0.18 and 0.24 (2 to 4 kappa1)
observable: dilute concentration u relative to saturation

regulation.change: the droplets removed: u = j/kappa1 follows the supply
